findings.title: Agent paused mid-reply for 2.31s, then resumed
findings.summary: At 5:15.8 the agent stopped speaking because of user voice activity that never produced a transcript, then resumed the same reply 2.31s later.

evidence.label: Agent reply affected
evidence.value: Thank you so much for your help. Goodbye.

evidence.label: User then asked the agent to repeat

root_cause.statement: Possible acoustic echo: the trigger began 0.35s after the agent started speaking, which fits the agent's own voice reaching the microphone.
missing_evidence: Microphone audio at the trigger time
The same script re-run with headphones

next_steps: Listen to the microphone channel at the trigger time.
Re-run the same script with headphones and compare false-interruption counts.
Lower false_interruption_timeout (default 2.0s) to shorten the gap, or raise min_interruption_duration if short sounds are the trigger.

findings.title: Agent output a stage direction: '(End of call)'
findings.summary: The agent's reply contains non-speech text, which the TTS reads aloud to the caller.

root_cause.statement: The LLM produced narration instead of speech; its instructions do not forbid this, and nothing filtered it before TTS.
missing_evidence: A re-run with an output filter (or stricter instruction) that no longer produces it

next_steps: Add an instruction: only output words to be spoken aloud.
Strip bracketed or parenthesized text before it reaches TTS.

findings.title: Agent replied to an unfinished sentence: 'In 3 weeks, Tuesday— sorry, um, Monday,'
findings.summary: The user turn was closed by the endpointing timeout and its transcript looks unfinished; the agent answered it anyway.

evidence.label: User turn (looks unfinished)
evidence.value: In 3 weeks, Tuesday— sorry, um, Monday,

evidence.label: Agent reply
evidence.value: Monday in three weeks... okay. What time would that be?

root_cause.statement: The user paused longer than the maximum endpointing delay mid-sentence, or the transcript dropped the end of the sentence.

next_steps: Listen to the turn to see whether the user had finished.
Check whether the next user turn completes this sentence.

findings.title: Agent could not make sense of 'Okay, okay. Um, no worries. So we are buying Patrick Swayze.'
findings.summary: The agent was confused by this transcript and the user then said they had said something else.

evidence.label: What the agent heard
evidence.value: Okay, okay. Um, no worries. So we are buying Patrick Swayze.

evidence.label: Agent could not make sense of it
evidence.value: I'm sorry, what? Who is Patrick Swayze? I'm trying to book an appointment with Dr. Patel.

evidence.label: User then corrected it
evidence.value: No, no, I said when is your appointment?

missing_evidence: Audio of the turn, or a reference transcript of what was said

next_steps: Listen to the turn and compare it with the transcript.
Check whether the user was speaking over the agent at the time.

findings.title: Session stayed open after both sides said goodbye; agent spoke 3 more time(s)
findings.summary: After the goodbye exchange nothing ended the call, so the agent kept responding to later input.

evidence.label: Goodbye
evidence.value: I just said thank you for your help, and goodbye.

evidence.label: Agent kept talking
evidence.value: Hello? I thought we had already finished the call. Did you need something else?

evidence.label: Agent kept talking
evidence.value: Hello? I'm still here. Is there something else you need?

root_cause.statement: The agent has no end-call action (no tool call appears in this session), so the session only ends when the other side disconnects.

next_steps: Give the agent an end-call tool and instruct it to use it after the goodbye exchange.
Re-run and check that the session closes right after the goodbye.

findings.title: 9 of 37 user turns ended by the 2.5s endpointing timeout
findings.summary: For these turns the turn detector never judged the user finished, so the agent waited the full 2.5s before replying.

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 4:30.4
evidence.value: 2.501s: 'Okay, okay. Um, no worries. So we are buying Patrick Swayze.'

evidence.label: Agent response latency after these turns

root_cause.statement: The user paused or trailed off mid-thought, so end-of-turn prediction stayed uncertain until the maximum delay.

next_steps: Read the timed-out turns: are they fragments or complete sentences?
If complete, check turn-detector settings; if fragments, the wait was correct.
Avoid lowering max_endpointing_delay blindly: it would cut users off mid-sentence.
